title: Detection of degradation of magnetic resonance (MR) images: comparison of an automated MR image-quality analysis system with trained human observers
reader_subset_verified: human reader not ascertainable at appraisal (abstract and MeSH basis); design label retained
rob_patient_selection_evidence: Parameters for imaging the test object and normal human volunteers were set to values that decreased the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), caused distortion, and increased the slice thickness and separation.
rob_patient_selection_rationale: Abstract only; volunteers and a test object are mentioned but no sampling rule, number of subjects, or inclusion/exclusion criteria are described.
rob_index_test_evidence: To evaluate the validity of this assumption, we compared the sensitivity of a test object and automated image analysis system for MR imaging QC with the sensitivity of trained human observers
rob_index_test_rationale: No statement about whether observers were blinded to which images had been degraded or to the degradation level, and no pre-specified detection threshold is reported.
rob_reference_standard_evidence: with the sensitivity of trained human observers by evaluating images that were intentionally degraded
rob_reference_standard_rationale: The ground truth was the experimentally applied degradation, which is known by construction and therefore classifies the target condition (presence/level of degradation) correctly.
rob_flow_timing_rationale: The abstract gives no information on how many images or observers entered the analysis, or whether any data were excluded.
app_patient_selection_evidence: Parameters for imaging the test object and normal human volunteers were set to values that decreased the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), caused distortion, and increased the slice thickness and separation.
app_patient_selection_rationale: A phantom test object plus normal volunteers, with no clinical brain-MRI patient population, does not match a review question about preserving diagnostic content in patients.
app_index_test_evidence: Automated analysis of test object images was able to detect all image degradations at the minimum levels applied.
app_index_test_rationale: The index test is deliberate parameter-driven degradation assessed by an automated QC system, not an accelerated or AI-based image reconstruction.
app_reference_standard_evidence: Further investigation is needed to better define the accuracy with which quantitative image-quality analysis predicts the effects of degraded image quality on the ability of human observers to detect subtle abnormalities in clinical images.
app_reference_standard_rationale: The authors explicitly state that the link between image-quality degradation and detection of clinical abnormalities was not established, so the reference does not address diagnostic content.
rater_status: verified
consensus_note: Independently appraised by three reviewers (2026-08-06); independent ratings agreed on all domains, no adjudication required.

rob_patient_selection_rationale: Sampling was purposive and pathology/artifact-enriched: UK Biobank images were deliberately selected by prior quality label, OASIS-3 cases were chosen to balance demented and healthy subjects, and MR-ART volunteers performed instructed head nodding, so the sample does not reflect a consecutive or random clinical stream.

rob_index_test_rationale: Checkpoint retention and final model selection (including choosing 3D-CNN-v2 and SVM-v1 for the headline comparison) used test-set performance, so the index-test threshold/configuration was not fully prespecified independently of the evaluation data, risking optimistic estimates.

rob_reference_standard_rationale: The reference was expert visual rating by five radiologists with senior revision and consensus discussion, performed blind to acquisition condition and before/independent of the model outputs, which is an acceptable truth standard for clinical usability.

design_detail: technical development and validation of a robust deep-generative-prior (untrained Deep Decoder) slice-to-volume reconstruction with diffeomorphic registration for whole-body fetal MRI, validated by synthetic/ablation experiments, LOOCV image metrics, single-radiologist paired preference rating, and a gestational-age prediction task
rob_patient_selection_evidence: We have tested our reconstruction algorithm in a cohort of 72 fetal cases consented as participants in the iFIND project
rob_patient_selection_rationale: The cohort mixes controls, suspected abnormalities, and incidental findings, but how the 72 cases were sampled from the iFIND project (consecutive, random, or purposive) and any inclusion/exclusion rules are not described.
rob_index_test_evidence: A radiologist with 11 years’ experience in fetal MRI was asked to select the higher quality image in each of three orthogonal pairs of matched slices extracted around the center of the trunk FOV from DSVR and RGDSVR.
rob_index_test_rationale: Blinding of the single reader to which method produced each image in the paired comparison is not reported, and several reconstruction hyperparameters were visually tuned on the same cohort, so independence of the index-test interpretation cannot be confirmed.
rob_reference_standard_evidence: The reconstruction with minimum data corruption as assessed by the average Normalized Cross Correlation (NCC) of adjacent input slices [11] is used as a synthetic GT
rob_reference_standard_rationale: No independent truth exists: the synthetic ground truth and the LOOCV agreement target are derived from the motion-corrupted acquired data and reconstructions themselves (incorporation bias), and the radiological assessment was a reference-free preference rating.
rob_flow_timing_evidence: Results of Peak SNR (PSNR), in dB, NCC and Structural SIMilarity Index (SSIM) are shown for all 72 cases in our cohort.
rob_flow_timing_rationale: All 72 cases were retrospectively reprocessed with every compared reconstruction method on the same acquisitions (zero interval, same reference procedure), and the radiologist preference covered all 72 cases (62 + 10) with no unexplained exclusions.
app_patient_selection_evidence: Magnetic resonance imaging of whole fetal body and placenta is limited by different sources of motion affecting the womb.
app_patient_selection_rationale: The population is fetal whole-body/placenta MRI at 20-36 weeks gestation, not the adult or clinical brain-MRI population targeted by the review; the fetal brain appears only as a secondary ROI for gestational-age prediction.
app_index_test_evidence: we propose a deep generative prior for robust volumetric reconstructions integrated with a diffeomorphic volume to slice registration method
app_index_test_rationale: The index test is a genuine DL-regularized reconstruction with hallucination-relevant generative prior, so it is task-relevant to reconstruction safety, but it is slice-to-volume motion-compensated reconstruction of the fetal body rather than reconstruction of undersampled k-space brain data.
app_reference_standard_evidence: lack of GT makes direct comparison of methods very challenging
app_reference_standard_rationale: The surrogate references used (NCC-selected synthetic ground truth, held-out corrupted stacks, and clinical-record gestational age acknowledged as error-prone) do not constitute a clinically relevant diagnostic truth standard for reconstruction safety.
